To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a visually guided system is able to grasp objects of arbitrary shapes and positions, even unknown a priori, in an industrial environment, with a low cost, high speed, and high reliability.
it is possible to grasp objects in a scene using a two-finger griper, and that it is possible with the same gripper to grasp unknown shapes in a scene.

a visually guided system using an inexpensive two- finger gripper can grasp arbitrary rectangular parts in an arbitrary position and orientation in the scene, can grasp arbitrary shaped parts, and can be deployed in an industrial setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system that can grasp objects in an industrial environment, using only a vision system as input and without any a priori knowledge of the objects.
the development and deployment of a system that is able to handle objects with a large variety of shapes in an online fashion.
the development of a vision-based robot system able to handle unknown objects in a flexible and efficient manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has shown how the vision-based system can handle objects with complex shapes and a priori unknown in industrial applications, opening up new areas of application.
vision-based object handling is a promising technology for industrial applications.
vision-based robot grasping is feasible in industrial applications, but the cost of the system and its reliability are still the main obstacles to its deployment in the industrial environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although we started from the idea of a visually guided robot for grasping objects, we have developed a general methodology to deal with a large variety of objects and scenes.

we have been able to demonstrate the feasibility of using vision as the sole source of information in order to achieve robust and flexible object manipulation, even in the presence of a large shape variability.
the system is robust and reliable enough to be used in industrial applications, and that its performance is comparable to the state of the art.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even though vision-based grasping has not yet been fully deployed in industrial applications, the technology is mature enough to be deployed in many cases.
the use of vision as input for grasping can be extended to a wider range of industrial applications than previously thought.
it is feasible to deploy a vision-based robot system in industry, even if it is not able to deal with all the situations that can be encountered.
